question:
A researcher tests for structural stability in the following regression model:

$y_t = \beta_1 + \beta_2 x_{2t} + \beta_3 x_{3t} + u_t$

The total sample of 200 observations is split exactly in half for the sub-sample regressions. Which would be the unrestricted residual sum of squares?
choice_a: The RSS for the whole sample
choice_b: The RSS for the first sub-sample
choice_c: The RSS for the second sub-sample
choice_d: The sum of the RSS for the first and second sub-samples

question: Suppose that the Durbin Watson test is applied to a regression containing two explanatory variables plus a constant with 50 data points. The test statistic takes a value of 1.53. What is the appropriate conclusion?
choice_a: Residuals appear to be positively autocorrelated
choice_b: Residuals appear to be negatively autocorrelated
choice_c: Residuals appear not to be autocorrelated
choice_d: The test result is inconclusive

question: Suppose that we have estimated a GARCH model for daily equity returns, and we are interested in producing a 10-day forecast of the volatility (measured by the standard deviation of returns) for use in a value at risk model. How could such a forecast most validly be calculated?
choice_a: Produce 1, 2, 3, ..., 10 step ahead conditional variance forecasts and add them up
choice_b: Produce 1, 2, 3, ..., 10 step ahead conditional variance forecasts and add them up and take the square root
choice_c: Produce 1, 2, 3, ..., 10 step ahead conditional variance forecasts, take the square roots of each one and add them up
choice_d: Produce a 1-step ahead conditional variance forecast, take its square root and multiply it by the square root of 10

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the acf and pacf?

(i) The acf and pacf are often hard to interpret in practice

(ii) The acf and pacf can be difficult to calculate for some data sets

(iii) Information criteria represent an alternative approach to model order determination

(iv) If applied correctly, the acf and pacf will always deliver unique model selections
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iii) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning maximum likelihood (ML) estimation in the context of GARCH models?

i) Maximum likelihood estimation selects the parameter values that maximise the

probability that we would have actually observed the values of the series y that we

actually did.


ii) GARCH models can only be estimated by ML and not by OLS


iii) For estimation of a standard linear model (with no GARCH), the OLS and ML

estimates for the slope and intercept parameters will be identical but the estimator

for the variance of the disturbances is slightly different


iv) Most computer packages use numerical procedures to estimate GARCH models

rather than a set of analytical formulae
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iii) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which of the following is an equivalent expression for saying that the explanatory variable is "non-stochastic"?
choice_a: The explanatory variable is partly random
choice_b: The explanatory variable is fixed in repeated samples
choice_c: The explanatory variable is correlated with the errors
choice_d: The explanatory variable always has a value of one

question: Under the null hypothesis of a Bera-Jarque test, the distribution has
choice_a: Zero skewness and zero kurtosis
choice_b: Zero skewness and a kurtosis of three
choice_c: Skewness of one and zero kurtosis
choice_d: Skewness of one and kurtosis of three.

question:
Which of the following are alternative names for the dependent variable (usually denoted by y) in linear regression analysis?

(i) The regressand

(ii) The regressor

(iii) The explained variable

(iv) The explanatory variable
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iii) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question:
Which of the following are plausible approaches to dealing with residual autocorrelation?

i) Take logarithms of each of the variables

ii) Add lagged values of the variables to the regression equation

iii) Use dummy variables to remove outlying observations

iv) Try a model in first differenced form rather than in levels.
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iii) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which one of the following is NOT an example of mis-specification of functional form?
choice_a: Using a linear specification when y scales as a function of the squares of x
choice_b: Using a linear specification when a double-logarithmic model would be more appropriate
choice_c: Modelling y as a function of x when in fact it scales as a function of 1/x
choice_d: Excluding a relevant variable from a linear regression model

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the Box-Jenkins approach to diagnostic testing for ARMA models?

(i) The tests will show whether the identified model is either too large or too small

(ii) The tests involve checking the model residuals for autocorrelation, heteroscedasticity, and non-normality

(iii) If the model suggested at the identification stage is appropriate, the acf and pacf for the residuals should show no additional structure

(iv) If the model suggested at the identification stage is appropriate, the coefficients on the additional variables under the overfitting approach will be statistically insignificant
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iii) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question:
Which of the following are disadvantages of the Dickey-Fuller / Engle-Granger approach to testing for cointegration and modelling cointegrating relationships?

i) Only one cointegrating relationship can be estimated

ii) Particularly for small samples. There is a high chance of the tests suggestingthat variables are not cointegrated when they are

iii) It is not possible to make inferences on the cointegrating regression

iv) The procedure forces the researcher to specify which is the dependent variable and which are the independent variables.
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iii) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: If OLS is applied separately to each equation that is part of a simultaneous system, the resulting estimates will be
choice_a: Unbiased and consistent
choice_b: Biased but consistent
choice_c: Biased and inconsistent
choice_d: It is impossible to apply OLS to equations that are part of a simultaneous system

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the standardised residuals (residuals divided by their respective conditional standard deviations) from an estimated GARCH model?

i) They are assumed to be normally distributed


ii) Their squares will be related to their lagged squared values if the GARCH model is

appropriate


iii) In practice, they are likely to have fat tails


iv) If the GARCH model is adequate, the standardised residuals and the raw residuals

will be identical
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iii) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question:
Which of the following statements are correct concerning the use of antithetic variates as part of a Monte Carlo experiment?

i) Antithetic variates work by reducing the number of replications required to cover the whole probability space

ii) Antithetic variates involve employing a similar variable to that used in the simulation, but whose properties are known analytically

iii) Antithetic variates involve using the negative of each of the random draws and repeating the experiment using those values as the draws

iv) Antithetic variates involve taking one over each of the random draws and repeating the experiment using those values as the draws
choice_a: (ii) and (iv) only
choice_b: (i) and (iii) only
choice_c: (i), (ii), and (iv) only
choice_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which one of the following criticisms of the Dickey-Fuller/Engle-Granger approach to dealing with cointegrated variables is overcome by the Engle-Yoo (EY) procedure?
choice_a: In the context of small samples, Dickey Fuller tests are prone to conclude that there is a unit root in a series when there is not
choice_b: The Engle-Granger (EG) approach can only detect up to one cointegrating relationship even though there could be more than one
choice_c: The variables are treated asymmetrically in the cointegrating tests
choice_d: It is not possible to perform tests about the cointegrating relationship

question: Consider a series that follows an MA(1) with zero mean and a moving average coefficient of 0.4. What is the value of the autocovariance at lag 1?
choice_d: It is not possible to determine the value of the autocovariances without knowing the disturbance variance.

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of continuously compounded returns (i.e. log-returns)?
choice_a: They can be interpreted as continuously compounded changes in the prices
choice_b: They can be added over time to give returns for longer time periods
choice_c: They can be added across a portfolio of assets to give portfolio returns
choice_d: They are usually fat-tailed

question: Which of the following statements is true concerning the population regression function (PRF) and sample regression function (SRF)?
choice_a: The PRF is the estimated model
choice_b: The PRF is used to infer likely values of the SRF
choice_c: Whether the model is good can be determined by comparing the SRF and the PRF
choice_d: The PRF is a description of the process thought to be generating the data.

question:
Consider the following sample autocorrelation estimates obtained using 250 data points:

1) Lag 1 2 3

2) Coefficient 0.2 -0.15 -0.1

3) Assuming that the coefficients are approximately normally distributed, which of the coefficients are statistically significant at the 5% level?
choice_a: 1 only
choice_b: 1 and 2 only
choice_c: 1, 2 and 3 only
choice_d: It is not possible to determine the statistical significance since no standard errors have been given

question: Automatic or built-in stabilizers
choice_a: prevent inflation.
choice_b: prevent recessions from occurring.
choice_c: prevent inflation and recessions from occurring.
choice_d: are government policies already in place that promote deficit spending during recessions and surplus budgets during expansions.

question: A budget deficit exists when
choice_a: the total amount that the government owes at a given time is positive
choice_b: government spending exceeds tax collections for a given period
choice_c: exports exceed imports in a given year
choice_d: imports exceed exports in a given year

question: Sue loses her job at a shoe factory when the economy falls into a recession. Sue is
choice_a: frictionally unemployed.
choice_b: cyclically unemployed.
choice_c: seasonally unemployed.
choice_d: structurally unemployed.

question: Suppose that current disposable income is $10000 and consumption spending is $8000. For every $100 increase in disposable income saving increases $10. Given this information
choice_a: the marginal propensity to consume is .80.
choice_b: the marginal propensity to save is .20.
choice_c: the marginal propensity to save is .10.
choice_d: the marginal propensity to save is .90.

question: According to Say's law
choice_a: when price goes up supply goes up
choice_b: it is better to give than receive
choice_c: demand creates its own supply
choice_d: supply creates its own demand

question: Suppose that Tiger Woods buys a golf ball in England for $1 and the marginal propensity to consume in England is 0.75. What is the total increase in England's real GDP resulting from Mr. Woods' purchase?
Which of the following is equal to one?
choice_a: The elasticity of the long-run aggregate supply curve
choice_b: The spending (or expenditure) multiplier
choice_c: The money (or banking) multiplier
choice_d: The balanced budget multiplier

question: A policy supported by supply-side economists would be
choice_a: higher taxes on corporate profits.
choice_b: lower tax rates on interest earned from savings.
choice_c: removal of investment tax credits.
choice_d: a longer duration of unemployment benefits.

question: Which of the following would reduce economic growth?
choice_a: A decline in investment.
choice_b: An increase in immigration from abroad.
choice_c: A technological advance.
choice_d: An increase in the labor force.

question: According to Keynesian analysis the Great Depression was caused by
choice_a: a lack of spending.
choice_b: a sharp rise in the marginal propensity to consume.
choice_c: too much investment.
choice_d: too much foreign influence on the economy.

question: What is the main contrast between the short-run and long-run Phillips curve?
choice_a: In the short run there is a positive relationship between inflation and unemployment and in the long run the relationship is negative.
choice_b: In the short run there is a positive relationship between inflation and unemployment and in the long run the relationship is constant.
choice_c: In the short run there is a negative relationship between inflation and unemployment and in the long run the relationship is positive.
choice_d: In the short run there is a negative relationship between inflation and unemployment and in the long run the relationship is constant.

question: Stagflation is the result of
choice_a: a leftward shift in the aggregate supply curve.
choice_b: a leftward shift in the aggregate demand curve.
choice_c: a leftward shift in both the aggregate supply and aggregate demand curves.
choice_d: a rightward shift in the aggregate supply curve.

question: If nominal GDP equals $5000 and real GDP equals $4000 then the GDP Deflator equals
It is unlikely that the unemployment rate will ever fall to zero because of
choice_a: frictional unemployment.
choice_b: cyclical unemployment.
choice_c: government policies.
choice_d: corporate policies.

question: When a bank's balance sheet shows that the bank has excess reserves
choice_a: the bank’s reserves exceed the bank’s assets
choice_b: the bank can make additional loans
choice_c: the bank’s actual reserves are less than its required reserves
choice_d: the bank is required to change its interest rate

question: Which of the following is not included in MI?
choice_a: Coins.
choice_b: Paper money.
choice_c: Travelers' checks.
choice_d: Credit cards.

question: U.S. real GDP most likely falls when
choice_a: tariffs and quotas are removed.
choice_b: investment in human capital is high.
choice_c: the money supply is increased.
choice_d: the value of the dollar relative to foreign currencies is high.

question: A difference between M1 and M2 is that
choice_a: M1 is a first mortgage and M2 is a second mortgage
choice_b: M2 is M1 plus assets that are more liquid
choice_c: M2 includes savings deposits
choice_d: M1 is larger than M2

question: According to Keynesian economists
choice_a: the investment demand curve is relatively elastic
choice_b: fiscal policy is more effective than monetary policy
choice_c: the economy is inherently stable
choice_d: inadequate supply is largely to blame for periods of stagnation

question: In the last 20 years firms that produce cameras have begun to produce fewer 35-mm cameras and more digital cameras. This trend is an example of
choice_a: how central planners dictate which cameras are produced.
choice_b: the market system answering the question of "how" cameras should be produced.
choice_c: the market system answering the question of "what" cameras should be produced.
choice_d: the market system answering the question of "who" should consume the cameras that are produced.

question: Which of the following statements is true for a firm in a perfectly competitive industry?
choice_a: Total revenue increases and then decreases.
choice_b: Marginal revenue is decreasing.
choice_c: Average revenue is initially negative and then becomes positive.
choice_d: Average revenue equals marginal revenue.

question: A competitive firm's demand for labor is determined directly by
choice_a: profits
choice_b: the opportunity cost of workers’ time
choice_c: the wage and the average (physical) product of labor
choice_d: the marginal (physical) product of labor and the output price

question: Elsa values her time at $50 per hour, and tutors David for two hours. David is willing to pay $175 for two hours of tutoring, but they negotiate a price of $125 for the entire two hours. Which of the following statements is true about the transaction above:
choice_a: Consumer surplus is greater than producer surplus by between $50 and $75.
choice_b: Producer surplus is greater than consumer surplus by between $50 and $75.
choice_c: Consumer surplus is greater than producer surplus by more than $75.
choice_d: The difference between consumer and producer surplus is $25.

question: Firms with the following market structure(s) maximize profits by producing where marginal cost equals marginal revenue, if at all. I. Perfect competition II. Oligopoly III. Monopoly IV. Monopolistic competition
choice_a: I only
choice_b: I and II only
choice_c: I and III only
choice_d: I, II, III, and IV

question: Good X is exchanged in a competitive market. Which of the following is true if an excise tax is now imposed on the production of good X?
choice_a: If the demand curve is perfectly elastic, the price rises by the amount of the tax.
choice_b: The consumer's burden of the tax rises as the demand curve is more elastic.
choice_c: Consumer surplus rises as a result of the tax.
choice_d: The consumer's burden of the tax rises as the demand curve is less elastic.

question: Relative to a competitive input market, a monopsony
choice_a: pays less and hires more
choice_b: pays less and hires the same amount
choice_c: pays more and hires more
choice_d: pays less and hires fewer

question: Monopolistic competition is said to be productively inefficient because
choice_a: the long-run price is above minimum average total cost.
choice_b: long-run profits are positive.
choice_c: firms engage in collusive behavior.
choice_d: there exist no barriers to entry.

question: With the presence of a positive externality, which of the following would correct the externality?
choice_a: A government subsidy.
choice_b: A government tax.
choice_c: A higher price.
choice_d: A lower level of output.

question: You are told that the income elasticity for DVDs is + 1.5. This means that
choice_a: a 10 percent increase in income produces a 15 percent increase in consumption of DVDs. DVDs are a normal luxury good.
choice_b: a 10 percent increase in income produces a 15 percent increase in consumption of DVDs. DVDs are an inferior good.
choice_c: a 10 percent increase in income produces a 15 percent decrease in consumption of DVDs. DVDs are an inferior good.
choice_d: a 10 percent increase in the price of DVDs produces a 15 percent decrease in consumption of DVDs. DVDs are a price elastic good.

question: Education makes Chris a better worker, voter, parent, and citizen. Because the benefits from education go beyond those that Chris enjoys himself, education provides
choice_a: increasing marginal utility and should be subsidized
choice_b: externalities and should be taxed
choice_c: decreasing marginal utility and should be taxed
choice_d: externalities and should be subsidized

question: The elasticity of supply is typically greater when
choice_a: producers have fewer alternative goods to produce.
choice_b: producers have less time to respond to price changes.
choice_c: producers are operating near the limits of their production.
choice_d: producers have more time to respond to price changes.

question: A monopoly is less efficient than a perfect competitor because
choice_a: a monopoly produces more output and sells for a higher price
choice_b: a monopoly produces less output and sells for a higher price
choice_c: a monopoly can make profit in the short run but not in the long run
choice_d: a perfect competitor breaks even in the short run and the monopoly does not

question: The market demand curve for labor will shift to the right when
choice_a: the number of firms increases
choice_b: the price of output decreases
choice_c: the labor supply curve shifts to the right
choice_d: the labor supply curve shifts to the left

question: Which of the following is most likely to result in a shift to the right in the demand curve for orange juice?
choice_a: A bumper crop of oranges in Florida
choice_b: A decrease in the price of Tang
choice_c: Expectations of lower future prices for orange juice
choice_d: Expectations of higher future income among juice drinkers

question: With respect to the kinked demand curve, which of the following is NOT correct?
choice_a: There is no price leader.
choice_b: There are relatively equal shares of the market.
choice_c: Price is greater than marginal costs.
choice_d: The demand curve is of one continuous function.

question: In a perfectly competitive market, a firm maximizes profit by producing the quantity at which:
choice_a: Total revenue equals total cost
choice_b: Marginal revenue equals marginal cost
choice_c: Average revenue equals average total cost
choice_d: Price equals average variable cost
context: Profit maximization condition in perfect competition

question: A bilateral monopoly exists when
choice_a: a monopsony buys from a monopoly
choice_b: a monopoly sells to two different types of consumers
choice_c: a monopoly buys from a monopsony
choice_d: a monopolist sells two different types of goods

question: Which of the following is true about a price floor?
choice_a: It is used to correct government policy.
choice_b: It is used when the equilibrium price is too high.
choice_c: It will be located above the equilibrium price.
choice_d: It will be located below the equilibrium price.

question: If firms are entering an industry that is monopolistically competitive, we would expect
choice_a: the demand for existing firms to shift rightward.
choice_b: the market price of the product to increase.
choice_c: the demand for existing firms to become more inelastic.
choice_d: the demand for existing firms to shift leftward.

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-run adjustment for the owners of a small café?
choice_a: The owners switch from whole wheat to sourdough bread.
choice_b: The owners hire several part-time workers to cover the dinner shifts.
choice_c: The owners work overtime on a busy weekend.
choice_d: The owners buy the office next door, and this doubles the customer seating.
